# ShiftMate synthetic dataset schema

**Status:** schema decision for the future generator; no data is generated by this document.  
**Schema version:** `1.0.0` · **Owner:** ShiftMate product/engineering · **Date:** 24 September 2026

## 1. Decision and boundaries

The generated dataset is a **relational bundle plus an append-only event stream**, not one wide CSV. A wide row cannot faithfully express a task with several waits, a corrected explanation, repeated alert transitions, missing signals, and two operators across shifts. The bundle serves four uses: (1) train and evaluate the task-time estimator, (2) supply comparable history for fair usage review, (3) replay safety and offline scenarios, and (4) seed a coherent demo. It does **not** represent real Cat telemetry or measured field performance.

`docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md` and `SHIFTMATE_PRODUCT_PLAN (1).md` contain the same product plan. The product plan controls behavior; `docs/TECHNICAL_SPEC.md` provides current runtime contracts. This schema deliberately expands its §8.22 generator outputs while preserving the eight named exports (`tasks.csv`, `idle_events.csv`, `alerts.csv`, `summaries_5m.csv`, `operators.csv`, `machines.csv`, `fleet.csv`, `manifest.json`). Implementation must update §8.22, T35, and their consumers to this version before generation. The user has authorized schema choices beyond the existing technical plan.

**Three kinds of information must remain distinct:**

1. **Pre-start inputs**: assignment, profile, operator experience at that date, and condition forecast available when the estimate was made. Only these are estimator features.
2. **Observed/reported events**: time-stamped signals, reports, task actions, detections, and alert transitions. Reports are claims until corroborated or reviewed; the latest correction changes the effective view without erasing history.
3. **Outcomes and oracle labels**: actual task duration/output and scripted `expect` results. They are available for training/evaluation **after** the event, never to the live estimator or rules under test.

**Notation:** `!` required, `?` nullable; `id` is a string key; `ts` is ISO 8601 UTC with millisecond precision; `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD` in site-local time; `int`, `float`, `bool`, and `str` have their usual JSON meanings. CSV numbers use a dot decimal and no thousands separators; booleans are `true`/`false`; nullable CSV fields are empty, never `0`, `unknown`, or `NA`. JSONL uses `null`. All numeric quantities are finite. Every file is UTF-8 with LF and a header for CSV. IDs and enum spellings match technical spec §5.1 unless explicitly named here.

## 2. Files, grain, and ownership

| File | One row/object per | Primary key | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest.json` | bundle | — | version, seed, origin, counts, checksums, splits |
| `sites.csv` | site | `site_id` | local time, sector, fuel and location context |
| `zones.csv` | site zone | `zone_id` | task location, speed limit, incident clustering |
| `operators.csv` | fictional operator | `operator_id` | experience, language, private learning boundary |
| `machines.csv` | detailed machine | `machine_id` | profile, class, age, site |
| `fleet.csv` | machine status snapshot | `machine_id` | 100-machine console view without fabricated detailed telemetry |
| `shifts.csv` | operator-machine shift | `shift_id` | chronology and comparable-history boundaries |
| `tasks.csv` | assigned task and final outcome | `task_id` | estimator training and outcome review |
| `conditions_hourly.csv` | site forecast valid hour | `condition_id` | weather/context with availability time |
| `summaries_5m.csv` | machine five-minute window | `summary_id` | history, fuel/cycle review, signal missingness |
| `idle_events.csv` | complete or open idle interval | `idle_event_id` | required/reported/unexplained time and attribution |
| `alerts.csv` | one alert lifecycle transition | `alert_event_id` | grouping, acknowledgment versus clearance |
| `ledger_entries.jsonl` | one append-only product event | `entry_id` | reports, corrections, task actions, estimates, findings, handover, learning |
| `incidents.jsonl` | incident projection at export time | `incident_id` | attributed fields and snapshot completeness |
| `proximity_events.jsonl` | scenario detection or heartbeat event | `proximity_event_id` | exact motion, quality, and feed availability for safety replay |
| `scenario_truth.jsonl` | scenario assertion | `truth_id` | independent safety/usage evaluation oracle, never an app input |
| `voice_test/utterances.jsonl` | labelled utterance | `utterance_id` | intent, slot, negation, and language tests |

**Separate authored artifacts:** `data/scenarios/*.yaml` remains the source for 1 Hz replay steps, including detection events and dropped/restored feeds; compiled scenarios follow technical spec §5.4.6. `packages/content/seed/demo_seed.json` stays the hand-authored demo reference source. `packages/content/seed/demo_history.json` is a deterministic projection from the bundle's last 14 days. `data/organiser/raw/` stays verbatim, outside generated files. An optional `signal_samples_1hz.jsonl` materialization is specified in §5 for debugging but is not needed for all 12 weeks.

The reference files do not duplicate secrets. Demo PIN hashes, console accounts, and pairing codes belong in `demo_seed.json`, not in the analytical dataset. `fleet.csv` contains a status snapshot for all 100 machines; `machines.csv` contains details for its 24 detailed machines. The remaining 76 fleet rows are status-only. This gives the console one complete fleet table without pretending all 100 have detailed telemetry.

Flat operational files are **projections**, not a second mutable truth: `summary_id` equals its `observation/signal_summary_5m` ledger `entry_id`; `alert_event_id` equals the corresponding `alert/*` ledger `entry_id` for device transitions; `idle_event_id` is the logical interval ID referenced by its start/end and reason entries. A human console review of an alert may appear in `alerts.csv` as `transition=reviewed` with its server audit ID; the device ledger has no `alert/reviewed` subtype.

## 3. Cross-cutting rules

### 3.1 Provenance and time

Every generated row has `data_origin! = synthetic:gen-1.0:<seed>` unless the schema says it is a demo seed, team recording or test oracle; `scenario_truth` instead has `data_origin! = scripted_challenge` or `synthetic:gen-1.0:<seed>`. Every operational record has `observed_at!` (when it happened) and `recorded_at!` (when it was saved), or the table's more precise `started_at`/`window_start` equivalent. Delivery/sync timing is a separate `received_at?`; it must never overwrite event time. Reference records use `created_at!`. Conditions use `issued_at!` and validity bounds because a forecast issued after a task starts cannot be used as a pre-start feature. Timestamps within each file sort ascending by the grain's time, then by ID.

The generator never silently fills missing signals. Sensor absence is represented by a missing signal or null value plus `missing_reason` and `last_seen_at`; stale is calculated from the last real timestamp and the machine profile's freshness limit. A zero speed, zero fuel, false belt state, and absent reading have different meanings.

Use stable UUID v4 syntax for generated shift/ledger/incident IDs; readable IDs for sites, zones, operators, machines, and tasks. For deterministic output, UUIDs may be generated from the seeded RNG; the bytes need not be cryptographically random. Foreign keys must resolve within this bundle or the declared demo seed. `scenario_truth` may reference a scenario-local ID when the matching runtime ID is created during replay.

### 3.2 Privacy and leakage

Use fictional names. No birth dates, demographic attributes, exact personal location tracks, real voice recordings, PINs, passwords, or raw free-text about a real person are generated. `operator_id` is an operational key, **not an estimator feature**. `language` supports UI/voice testing, **not speed prediction**. Individual hidden operator effects may be used by the generator, but they are documented in assumptions and are not exported as model inputs. Private `learning_event` entries have `audience=operator_only` and are excluded from server sync exports.

`tasks.csv` has a documented **feature cutoff** at `estimate_requested_at`. Columns under “outcome” cannot appear in training X, even if the CSV stores them beside features. Likewise `idle_events`' final reason, incident outcome, alert transitions, and the scenario oracle cannot be joined to pre-start predictions. Split A is weeks 1–8 train, 9–10 calibration, 11–12 test; split B holds out eight fixed operators as in technical spec §8.22. The `split_*` columns are metadata, never features. Comparable-history features must be computed only from events before the prediction time.

## 4. Exact column dictionary

### 4.1 Reference and schedule

**`sites.csv`** — one site. Values come from the demo seed, so these rows may use `data_origin=demo_seed` rather than a synthetic generator origin.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `site_id!` | id | Foreign key for conditions, tasks, zones and fair same-site comparisons. |
| `name!` | str | Human-readable briefing and console label. |
| `sector!` | enum `construction/mining` | Keeps excavator and haul contexts separate. |
| `lat!`, `lon!` | float | Approximate fictional site placement for demo map/SOS; no operator track. |
| `utc_offset_minutes!` | int | Converts UTC events to site-local shift date and time-of-day. |
| `diesel_price_inr_per_l!` | float | Labels the idle fuel-cost suggestion with the site's assumption. |
| `dark_start_local!`, `dark_end_local!` | `HH:MM` | Darkness modifier and night UI context. |
| `job_efficiency_override?` | float `(0,1]` | Optional site-specific baseline assumption; null uses profile default. |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Auditable source and chronology. |

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `zone_id!`, `site_id!` | id, id | Zone identity and site guard. |

| `center_lat!`, `center_lon!`, `radius_m!` | float, float, float `>0` | Fictional geofence context for demos; not a safety certified boundary. |
| `speed_limit_kmh?` | float `>0` | Overspeed rule for haul roads; null means no zone-specific limit. |
| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Provenance. |

**`operators.csv`** — 48 fictional operators. Experience is also snapshotted on each task to avoid using a later value for an earlier job.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `operator_id!`, `site_id!` | id, id | Shift assignment and site-scoped history. |
| `display_name!` | str | Fictional demo display only. |
| `language!` | `en/hi/ta` | Voice/content routing; excluded from estimator X. |
| `skill_level!` | `beginner/intermediate/expert` | Guidance defaults and estimator feature. |

| `data_origin!`, `created_at!` | str, ts | Provenance. |

| Column | Type | Why it exists |

**`fleet.csv`** — status snapshot for all 100 machines. Twenty-four rows link to `machines.csv`; the other 76 have no detailed task or 1 Hz history. The console reads this table directly.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |

### 4.2 Estimator table: `tasks.csv`

One row is an assignment plus its final outcome. **A completed row is training eligible only when `actual_active_min>0`, required pre-start inputs are available, and task/profile/unit are supported.** Cancelled or open rows still matter to the task board and should not be dropped. No per-cycle metrics are required to train time prediction.

| Column | Type | Why it exists / availability |
|---|---|---|
| `task_id!`, `assignment_revision!` | id, int `>=1` | Stable assignment key and revision; revision is not an ML feature. |
| `site_id!`, `zone_id?`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id!`, `shift_id?` | ids | Assignment and comparable context; shift may be unknown before sign-in. |
| `task_type!`, `material!`, `quantity!`, `unit!` | str, str, float `>0`, Unit | Baseline rate and model features; unit must match profile task type. |
| `location_text!`, `priority!`, `completion_criterion!` | str, int `1..3`, str | Task board and explicit definition of done; excluded from v1 estimator. |
| `assignment_source!` | `dispatcher/seed/reassignment` | Audit who assigned work. |
| `planned_date!`, `planned_start_at!`, `estimate_requested_at!` | date, ts, ts | Scheduling, feature cutoff, and exact forecast join. |
| `planner_minutes?` | float `>0` | Fair same-task baseline comparison; never a generated estimator target. |
| `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | id, int | Freeze baseline constants used on that task. |
| `skill_level_at_start!`, `experience_months_at_start!`, `machine_age_years_at_start!` | enum, int, int | Features as known then; avoids joining future operator/machine state. |
| `condition_id?`, `weather_at_start?`, `visibility_at_start?`, `temperature_band_at_start?`, `time_of_day_at_start!`, `site_congestion_at_start?` | id/enums | Pre-start context. Null is honest; runtime fallback is separate from stored raw context. Forecast must have `issued_at<=estimate_requested_at`. |
| `baseline_minutes?` | float `>0` | Recomputed from the frozen profile, quantity, material and job efficiency; null when unsupported. |
| `status!` | TaskState | Board lifecycle; outcome fields stay null until completed. |
| `actual_start_at?`, `actual_end_at?` | ts | Outcome chronology, not pre-start features. |
| `actual_active_min?`, `actual_waiting_min?`, `actual_break_min?`, `actual_paused_min?`, `actual_elapsed_min?` | float `>=0` | Work/wait separation, accounting checks and training target (`actual_active_min` only). |
| `output_qty?` | float `>=0` | Completion confirmation and realised production. |
| `completion_quality!` | `confirmed/partial/unverified/not_applicable` | Prevents treating an unverified completion as clean training truth. |
| `training_eligible!`, `training_exclusion_reason?` | bool, str | Reproducible inclusion policy; exclusion reason required when false. |
| `split_temporal!`, `split_unseen_operator!` | `train/calibration/test/excluded` | Explicit fixed evaluations; metadata only. |
| `data_origin!`, `recorded_at!` | str, ts | Synthetic disclosure and late outcome receipt. |

`actual_elapsed_min` equals `(actual_end_at-actual_start_at)` in minutes for completed work, within rounding tolerance. It can include active, waiting, break and paused time; account for any residual as `unclassified_min` **only if needed**, then document why. `actual_active_min` is the Ridge target, not wall-clock elapsed. `output_qty` may be below `quantity` for a partial completion; such a row is not training eligible by default. Baseline and planner estimates stay as they were at start. Live estimate changes are ledger entries, never overwritten into this row.

### 4.3 Conditions and machine observations

**`conditions_hourly.csv`** — one issued forecast for a site and validity hour; multiple issuances may overlap. This is an input record, not proof that rain occurred.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `condition_id!`, `site_id!` | ids | Stable join to a task's available forecast. |
| `valid_from!`, `valid_to!`, `issued_at!` | ts | Temporal join and leakage prevention; half-open interval `[from,to)`. |
| `weather!`, `visibility!` | product enums | Estimator and risk notes. |
| `visibility_m?` | float `>=0` | Supports reproducible visibility banding; null when only a category exists. |
| `temp_c!`, `heat_index_c?`, `wind_kmh!`, `precipitation_mm!` | floats | Heat/wind/rain rules with explicit units. |
| `source!` | `seed/open_meteo` | Matches the runtime forecast contract. Generated forecasts use `seed`; a live operator condition report is a separate ledger entry, never backdated into the forecast. |
| `data_origin!`, `recorded_at!` | str, ts | Origin and availability. |

**`summaries_5m.csv`** — derived only from readings actually present within a half-open five-minute window. These rows reproduce the technical ledger `observation/signal_summary_5m` payload; optional context fields aid analysis but do not change it.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `summary_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?` | ids | Window identity and contextual comparison. |
| `window_start!`, `window_end!`, `recorded_at!` | ts | Exact interval and receipt. |
| `engine_on_s!`, `secured_s!`, `ready_s!`, `working_s!`, `travelling_s!`, `unknown_s!`, `idle_s!` | ints `0..300` | Utilisation and conservative unknown state; state seconds sum to at most window length. |
| `fuel_used_l?`, `load_cycles?`, `max_speed_kmh?`, `avg_load_factor_pct?`, `belt_unfastened_moving_s?` | floats/ints | Fuel per cycle, overspeed and belt history; nullable if signal unavailable. |
| `samples!`, `missing_samples!` | ints `0..300` | Makes coverage visible; `samples+missing_samples=300` for a full window. |
| `missing_signal_names!` | JSON string array | Names what was absent, not just how many timestamps are absent. |
| `profile_id!`, `profile_version!`, `data_origin!` | id, int, str | Rule/rate interpretation and origin. |

No cumulative fuel or engine-hour reading is interpolated. `fuel_used_l` is interval consumption only if both endpoints exist and pass monotonicity/quality checks; otherwise null. A 5-minute summary cannot support a two-second safety decision and must not be fed into the seatbelt/proximity rule engine.

**`signal_samples_1hz.jsonl` (optional materialized replay)** — one actual simulator tick for a scenario, not a 12-week stream. Keys: `scenario_id!`, `sample_id!`, `machine_id!`, `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!`, `signals!` (object of name → typed value), `last_seen_at!` (object of name → ts), `missing_reason?` (object of name → `dropout/not_equipped/not_emitted`), `data_origin!`. Signal names/types are taken from profile JSON and technical spec §5.4.1. Omitted signal means no fresh reading, **not** a default false/zero. This file is a debug export; scenario YAML remains the replay source.

**`proximity_events.jsonl`** — one scenario detection or feed heartbeat event. This is a projection of authored YAML steps; it does not invent a detected person during a feed outage. Keys: `proximity_event_id!`, `scenario_id!`, `machine_id!`, `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!`, `event_type!` (`detection/heartbeat/feed_off/feed_on`), `object_id?`, `object_type?`, `bearing_deg?`, `distance_m?`, `closing_mps?`, `sensor_quality?`, `last_heartbeat_at?`, `data_origin!`. Detection rows require object, bearing (0–360° relative to machine front), nonnegative distance, signed closing speed (positive = approaching), and quality (0–1). Feed events carry no object fields. This matches F7's inputs and makes approaching/departing and stale-feed pairs inspectable; threshold decisions are produced by the rule engine, not stored as detection truth.

### 4.4 Idle and alert projections

**`idle_events.csv`** — one idle interval, derived from signal/task events and linked to its report entry when there is one. The class is an inference and may change after correction; this CSV is the **effective view at export**, while ledger history keeps the original and corrections.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `idle_event_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id?`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?`, `zone_id?` | ids | Joins wait to task, site follow-up and operator-private review. |
| `started_at!`, `ended_at?`, `recorded_at!` | ts | Interval; null end means ongoing. |
| `duration_s?`, `required_s!`, `non_required_s?` | ints `>=0` | Separates warm-up/cool-down/regen from potentially explainable time. |
| `required_basis!` | `warmup/cooldown/regen/mixed/none` | Explains why an idle was required; no operator blame. |
| `idle_class!` | `required/reported/unexplained` | Rule result; `reported` must point to a reason entry. |
| `reason_code?`, `reason_entry_id?`, `reason_recorded_at?` | enum, id, ts | Operator claim and when it arrived; null for required/unexplained. |
| `category?` | `site_delay/break/other` | Fair time accounting and routing, derived from reason. |
| `prompted_at?`, `prompt_answered_at?` | ts | Measures interruption and delayed explanation. |
| `sensor_coverage_pct!` | float `0..100` | Marks uncertain classification if required signals were missing. |
| `evidence_status!` | EvidenceStatus | Reported, corroborated or insufficient evidence; never silently factual. |
| `data_origin!` | str | Provenance. |

**`alerts.csv`** — one transition per alert, so acknowledgment cannot erase an active hazard. Device transitions come from ledger `alert/*` entries; optional `reviewed` transitions come from the server review/audit record.

| Column | Type | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `alert_event_id!`, `alert_id!`, `site_id!`, `machine_id!`, `shift_id?`, `task_id?`, `zone_id?` | ids | Transition identity, grouping, scope and context. |
| `transition!` | `raised/escalated/acknowledged/cleared/reviewed` | Full lifecycle. |
| `alert_type!`, `level!` | tech §5.1 enums | Reproduces rule output and severity. |
| `group_key!`, `occurrences!` | str, int `>=1` | One cause can raise repeated detections without alert spam. |
| `object_id?`, `object_type?`, `place?` | ids/enums | Proximity explanation; null for belt/speed/etc. |
| `distance_m?`, `ttc_s?`, `zone_multiplier?` | floats | Explains why a proximity threshold fired; not required for other alerts. |
| `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!`, `received_at?` | ts | Rule time, device save time, later sync. |
| `source!` | `observed/reported/reviewed` | Raise/clear is observed, acknowledge is reported, review is reviewed. |
| `rule_or_model_version!`, `profile_id!`, `profile_version!` | str, id, int | Threshold auditability. |
| `data_origin!` | str | Provenance. |

### 4.5 Canonical event stream and incidents

**`ledger_entries.jsonl`** follows technical spec §5.3.1 *exactly* for the runtime object: `entry_id!`, `device_id!`, `shift_id?`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id?`, `kind!`, `subtype!`, `source!`, `payload!`, `observed_at!`, `recorded_at!`, `freshness_s?`, `confidence?`, `rule_or_model_version?`, `original_text?`, `supersedes?`, `audience!`, `data_origin!`, `sync_status!`, `chain_seq?`, `prev_hash?`, `content_hash?`, `canonical_payload?`. In this file timestamps are ISO UTC strings; importer converts them to device epoch milliseconds. `payload` is validated by technical spec §5.3.2, not a free-form bag. The mandatory generated kinds are:

| Kind/subtype | Why include it in generated history |
|---|---|
| `shift_event/start,end`; `task_event/start,pause,resume,block,complete,cancel` | Rebuild task chronology and handover without trusting `tasks.csv` alone. |
| `observation/signal_summary_5m`, `observation/condition_forecast` | Seed comparable usage and time-aware conditions. |
| `idle_event/started,ended`; `report/idle_reason`; `correction/idle_reason` | Show explain-once propagation and corrected attribution. |
| `report/progress_report`, `inference/estimate` | Live ETA changes with source/version and original estimate retained. |
| `alert/raised,escalated,acknowledged,cleared`; `incident/created,snapshot_completed`; `report/incident_report` | Safety independent of explanation, and 60 s pre/30 s post snapshots. |
| `inference/finding`, `inference/recommendation`, `report/recommendation_feedback` | Fair routing and relevance tests; private entries stay local. |
| `handover_item/added,edited,acknowledged,resolved` | Acknowledged remains open until resolved. |
| `learning_event/started,answered,completed,deferred` | Private learning flow only, never in server exports. |

The `source` enum (`observed/reported/inferred/reviewed`) describes **epistemic status**; `data_origin` describes **where this record came from**. They are not interchangeable. Reports preserve `original_text` only for fictional synthetic utterances. A correction points to `supersedes` and carries the replacement payload, even if it retracts an earlier report. Incident ledger entries require the specified chain fields and valid hashes. Generated history does not fake server `received_at`; the importer/sync test adds it when delivery occurs.

**`incidents.jsonl`** is a materialized projection, never a substitute for its ledger source. Keys: `incident_id!`, `site_id!`, `zone_id?`, `machine_id!`, `operator_id?`, `shift_id?`, `occurred_at!`, `created_at!`, `origin!` (`auto/operator`), `trigger_alert_id?`, `type?`, `severity?`, `status!` (`awaiting_report/reported/reviewed`), `fields!` (each `{value,source,entry_id}` as technical spec §5.3.3), `snapshot!` (technical spec `Snapshot` with pre/post samples and proximity/alerts), `snapshot_complete!`, `reviewed_at?`, `chain_ok!`, `data_origin!`. This projection makes missing context and field-by-field attribution visible to the safety/trainer flows. A reported near miss is not automatically a verified contact or injury.

### 4.6 Evaluation-only labels and voice

**`scenario_truth.jsonl`** is an independent assertion manifest, not a telemetry or training file. Keys: `truth_id!`, `scenario_id!`, `pair_id?`, `variant!`, `evaluated_at_s?`, `expectation!` (the exact `expect` object from §5.4.6), `rationale!`, `author_role!` (`generator_author/independent_challenge_author`), `data_origin!`. The independent challenge author must write their own cases; copying the generator's thresholds into the oracle makes safety metrics circular. Scenarios include all ten product §13.5 pairs/challenges, especially missing lockout, stale proximity feed, wait correction, and offline sync.

**`voice_test/utterances.jsonl`** — ~150 fictional text utterances, with optional team-recorded audio kept in a separate consented asset folder. Keys: `utterance_id!`, `language!` (`en/hi`, optional `ta`), `text!`, `intent!`, `slots!` (object with expected values), `negated!`, `should_create_record!`, `expected_confirmation!`, `context_state!` (MachineState), `split!` (`train/test/challenge`), `source!` (`synthetic_text/team_recorded`), `audio_asset_id?`, `review_status!` (`draft/human_reviewed`), `data_origin!`. The audio asset ID is a reference, not a transcript guarantee. English/Hindi performance is reported separately; Tamil is not claimed until supported/reviewed.

## 5. Generation and validation contract for the later phase

The future generator should create a small latent event timeline first, then emit truthful observations/reports and deterministic projections. In particular, a truck queue may cause an idle, but the **reported reason** can be late, absent or corrected; rule outputs must be recomputed from visible inputs. Generate realistic correlations (weather ↔ visibility, material ↔ production, congestion ↔ waits, signal faults ↔ missing data) without making them perfectly deterministic. Include counterexamples so a model cannot simply learn the generator's equation or infer blame from operator identity. Publish every effect and range in `docs/GENERATOR_ASSUMPTIONS.md`; label illustrative safety thresholds as such. Values in technical spec §8.22 are starting assumptions, not measured Cat coefficients.

`manifest.json` must contain `schema_version`, `generator_version`, `seed`, `anchor_date`, `generated_at` (fixed/reproducible for byte-identical builds), `data_origin`, `profile_versions`, `files` (`path`, `rows`, `sha256`, `grain`), `split_policy`, `assumptions_sha256`, and `limitations`. `--effect-scale 0.5/1.5` gets separate manifests and directories. Sort rows and JSON keys canonically, fix float precision and line endings, and exclude machine-specific wall-clock timestamps from deterministic outputs.

Validation gates before any model training:

1. Every file parses; the manifest hashes/counts match; fixed seed yields identical bytes; different seed differs.
2. Keys are unique; foreign keys resolve; `fleet.csv` has 100 distinct machines with 24 `detailed` rows matching `machines.csv` and 76 `status_only` rows; 48 operators; about 2,500 tasks; site/class/task/profile/unit combinations are valid.
3. Times respect chronology: forecast issued by estimate time, report no earlier than event, correction after original, alert clear after raise, incident post-snapshot after trigger, handover acknowledgment after item creation.
4. Task accounting is consistent to rounding; active target is positive for training rows; no outcome, reason, alert, or oracle field enters pre-start feature encoding.
5. Sensor dropouts produce `UNKNOWN`/unavailable according to profile freshness; absence is never normal. Required cool-down, reported wait and unexplained idle produce distinct labels. Acknowledging an active alert does not clear it.
6. `scenario_truth` and challenge utterances stay outside model training; temporally held-out and unseen-operator evaluations use the declared fixed splits.
7. Organiser files remain untouched. Their original rows are mapped separately with a documented mapping and no invented lockout/seat-occupancy state.

## 6. Why these fields, and what remains an assumption

| Design choice | Product consequence | Evidence / status |
|---|---|---|
| Quantity, material, machine profile, job efficiency, cycles/payload and dated conditions are separate fields. | Baseline and correction can be explained independently; the app can compare a planner estimate on the same task. | Cat's Performance Handbook gives a job-efficiency table and bucket payload method; its factors are planning examples, **not** the generator's validated coefficients. [Cat Performance Handbook, ed. 50](https://wheelercat.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Cat-Performance-Handbook-Edition-50-June-2022.pdf), [Cat wheel-loader productivity guidance](https://www.cat.com/en_US/articles/for-owners/how-to-calculate-cat-wheel-loader-productivity.html). |
| Work, wait, break and pause are separate from wall-clock elapsed. | A reported site delay changes finish time and attribution without falsely slowing the operator's active rate. | ShiftMate F4/F9; Cat VisionLink also distinguishes working/idle time, cycles, payload and fuel at machine/site level. [VisionLink Productivity](https://www.cat.com/en_US/products/new/technology/visionlink/visionlink/132084.html). |
| Event time, receipt time, forecast issuance and missingness are explicit. | Offline sync, stale-signal safety and historical estimates stay reproducible. | ShiftMate principles 4–5 and F13; ISO/TS 15143-3 defines server-side telematics exchange, **not** on-board CAN collection, so this schema does not pretend to be an ISO CAN format. [ISO/TS 15143-3:2020](https://www.iso.org/standard/76394.html). |
| Proximity episodes have relative object motion, type, position, quality and independent oracle labels in scenario artifacts. | Can test approaching/departing, nuisance alarms and feed outages, rather than accuracy on a distance-only rule. | NIOSH distinguishes true, nuisance, false and missed alarms and emphasizes situational context. Its study does **not** validate ShiftMate's illustrative distances. [NIOSH surface-mining recommendations](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/docs/mining/UserFiles/works/pdfs/2007-146.pdf). |
| Synthetic provenance is inside each row as well as in the manifest; sensitivity and challenge cases are separate. | Demo/evaluation cannot accidentally be presented as field results; circular test design is visible. | ShiftMate principles 13 and §17.2; NIST recommends evaluating synthetic data against intended use and documents the distinction between synthetic and real records. [NIST synthetic-data guide](https://pages.nist.gov/HLG-MOS_Synthetic_Data_Test_Drive/guide.html). |

**Still assumed, pending generation:** exact effect sizes, distribution shapes, missing-signal rates, condition transition probabilities, report latency, wait frequency, and acceptable challenge coverage. They must live in versioned generator config with rationales and sensitivity runs. This schema fixes the *meaning and structure* of data, not a claim that those parameter values are true on a real site.
